description.p: CaraStudio is an open-source program to read and manipulate RAW images from digital cameras.

To get the best quality out of your digital camera, it is often recommended that you record your pictures in RAW format. This format is mostly specific to a camera and cannot be read by most image editing applications. Our goal is to supply you with a tool, where you can have the benefits of RAW images and the ease of use of JPEG images.

The main focus of CaraStudio is to enable efficient review and fast processing of large image collections. We aim to supply you with a tool that makes it possible for you to review and process several hundred images in a matter of a few hours.

Color balance: the three wheels are larger and redrawn, with an outer chromatic ring and a centre that lightens towards white. The chosen hue direction is now remembered even when the intensity is brought back to zero, stays marked on the ring, and is preserved from one session to the next. The tool panel divider is set from the real window allocation, and a few Gtk-CRITICAL messages emitted when closing a photo are gone.

Interface themes: a Theme selector in Preferences offers CaraStudio (the original palette), Studio Anthracite, Studio Clair and Studio Ambre, applied instantly without restarting. The Color balance wheels gain permanent Hue, Intensity and Luminance sliders, kept in sync with the wheels both ways. The three wheels are now weighted on perceived luminance, which makes the Highlights wheel effective again; photos already developed using these wheels will render slightly differently. Lens correction: the lens database bundled in the AppImage is finally loaded, so users without lensfun installed are no longer left without any recognised lens. The camera database no longer fills up with empty entries and cleans itself up. Saving camera defaults now asks for confirmation and offers to clear existing defaults. The manual documents every menu, the Edit menu and the new features, in French and English. Themes and wheel sliders contributed by Christian Bouhon.

Crop and straighten moved into a dedicated tool-panel module (ART style): a toolbar Straighten button (press again to undo), a Crop button that collapses the other modules and brings the crop controls to the top, and Cancel that always removes the crop. Several old crop/straighten crashes inherited from RawStudio are fixed. Fujifilm X-Trans (.raf) files no longer open over-exposed.

New Enfuse button, a 4-tab Curves block with per-channel RGB curves and curve presets, auto-exposure / auto-levels / reset in Basic, a white balance exposure mask, the Pipeline legend with A-E stage badges, and a richly illustrated in-app help (F1) in French and English.
